source: Yemeni government / AFP military source / Houthi claim
note: Government confirmed 30 killed, 50 wounded across Homeland Shield Forces, Emergency Forces and First Military Region camps; an unnamed military source told AFP the toll may reach 58; Houthis claim 45 killed. Deadliest single episode of the conflict in years — troops were gathered for a morning training exercise when struck.

source: Saudi Press Agency / Saudi-led Coalition Joint Forces Command
note: 7 Saudi citizens (incl. a woman and a 4-year-old with 2nd-degree burns), 1 Yemeni, 2 Egyptians, 1 Pakistani wounded. Highest civilian toll inside Saudi Arabia in over four years.

category: Maritime — Tihamah Crew & Rescuers (Bab al-Mandeb, Aug 11)
source: Al Jazeera / ABC News (Australia) / NBC News
note: 4 crew killed (3 Pakistani, 1 Indonesian) in the initial 'double-tap' strike; a second missile on the search-and-rescue operation killed 2 Yemeni coast guard rescuers and wounded several more. First fatal Houthi attack on shipping since the Iran war began Feb 28.
Houthis say they targeted weapons/warship buildups of Saudi-backed forces and 'mercenaries'; government characterizes the toll as civilian.

source: Yemeni government / unnamed military official via AFP / Al Jazeera
note: Government's initial count was 4 civilians killed and fishing boats set ablaze; an unnamed government military official told AFP the toll reached at least 8, including 2 security personnel.
Six ballistic missiles and four drones struck residential neighborhoods and displacement camps in Marib, a city hosting 2M+ displaced people.

category: Saudi Landing Ship Crew (Mokha, Aug 17 — claimed)
note: Houthis claim the landing ship was 'completely burned' with escort boats sunk/ablaze. Yemen's government disputes the vessel's identity, saying it was a decommissioned commercial ship under maintenance. No Saudi confirmation and no casualty figures released by any party.

source: Yemeni Armed Forces spokesmen (Col. Majed al-Nazili, Gen. Majid Abdullah al-Nuzaili)
note: Government said 181 operations on Aug 16 and 81 more on Aug 20 killed or wounded dozens of Houthi fighters and commanders and destroyed equipment across multiple fronts. One-sided government tally with no independent verification of casualty figures.

category: Civilians Killed by US Strikes (Operation Rough Rider, 2025)
note: 3 April 2025 US strikes reviewed by the Pentagon 'more likely than not' caused civilian harm; report released Aug 11, 2026, the Trump administration's first public acknowledgment of significant civilian harm from US operations. No condolence payments approved; 15 further incidents under investigation.

source: UN Development Programme / UN News, Dec 2021 (pre-2026 escalation)
note: ~60% from indirect causes (famine, disease, lack of healthcare). Saudi-led coalition disputes indirect-cause methodology; ACLED's narrower direct-violence tally separately recorded 70,000+ direct fatalities. Figure pre-dates and will be revised by the 2026 escalation.

source: UN OCHA — Yemen Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
note: Part of 22M+ Yemenis requiring humanitarian assistance in 2026. Displacement from Hadramawt to Marib alone rose by 1,634 households amid the August 2026 escalation. The 2026 aid appeal is barely 20% funded.
